about: Product facts the history checkers read. A row that states a number carries its cite (a page or source line at read_at). If the pages change a number, this file changes with them, never the checker.

reader.about: The product's code for reading an observation and placing an operation from it: checkers/product_block.py, loaded by file (the checkers run under python -I).

bounds_note: C6 latency bounds, rows of {verb, seconds, cite}. The operator pages state no bound on the duration of any operation, so there is no row and every verb is listed as not judged. Only a bound a page states goes here, never an invented number.

recovery.what: a holder that crashed is re-granted at most this long after it stopped
the holder's start wait ends this long after the re-grant or after its start, whichever is later

recovery_note: A holder is healthy again by max(kill completion + regrant, restart completion) + start_wait. The pages state no restart bound for the master: its restart is not judged.

master_outage.what: volumes already serving keep serving through a master restart this short: each holder renews every 10 s or less and may serve until 20 s after its last renewal, so a master that answers again within 10 s interrupts nothing. A longer outage is not judged by MO (it is fail-closed, with its own recovery bound).

holder_unit.what: the product's shipped unit for blockvolume. The runner plays it for every holder it launched and reads its policy (Restart, RestartPreventExitStatus, RestartSec, TimeoutStopSec) from this file at the product commit the run built, never from a copy here; if the file cannot be read or parsed, it refuses to emulate. A holder the runner killed itself is left to the fault schedule's restart.

fault_targets.name: blockmaster
fault_targets.what: the block master daemon; a kill of it reaches no holder, so no volume's data path

fault_targets.name: blockvolume:<i>
fault_targets.what: the block volume daemon holding volume i (from 0); a process whose name starts with the prefix is a holder

block_bytes.what: the block size in bytes on first create (the daemon's --durable-blocksize default; the runner also passes 4096); the checkers' ZERO is the sha256 of one block of zeros

time_derived.cite: cmd/sw-block/workspace_show.go:54-58 (expired exactly when the validity is <= 0, else revoking or granted), :60 (the expiry and the validity at query); docs/volume-lifecycle.md:35
time_derived.why: the lease state is derived from a fact (the lease's expiry) and the clock: it is the host validity at query time. A step listed here is time alone only when the fact is equal in both observations, the earlier observation's validity is not larger than the longest time that can lie between the two readings (the later observation's end, mono_ns, minus the earlier one's start, from_mono_ns), and every other kept fact is equal. Otherwise, and for any step not listed (time does not run backwards: expired to granted), it stays a change. An observation without from_mono_ns gives no bound, so no step is time alone.

observation.required_note: C5 requires these parts in both observations of a judged refusal: a pair lacking one leaves the refusal not judged (no PASS on what was not seen).

ignored.field: head: VolumeID, ClaimID, Activity, Current, Position
ignored.why: not recorded by the observation: it keeps HEAD's generation, epoch, holder and state, the volume's identity, ownership and life state

ignored.field: head.Snapshots: each snapshot's root and position
ignored.why: only the snapshot names are compared; the volume's root objects appear in the file listing (files)
only the error code is compared: the exit status of a failed show says no more than its code

ignored.field: snapshots_error, dirs_error, listing_error, an unreadable head
ignored.why: not values: a part recorded with an error cannot be compared, and a refusal judged on it is left not judged
changes with every renewal; not a state a refusal can change. Not compared; kept only as the fact the lease state derives from (time_derived)
changes with every query; not a state a refusal can change. Not compared; kept only to bound a time_derived step
